A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same privacy-memorization study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be reliably matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA evaluations, gradient comparisons, representation visualizations, layer-wise probing results and a batch-size ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds membership-inference evaluations and experiments varying training steps, model capacity and privacy-subset size.

M1.justification: The watermark-based fine-tuning procedure and layer-wise binary probing framework in Section 3 remain unchanged. v2 applies the existing procedure under additional experimental configurations without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 4.4 adds a dedicated synthetic member/non-member evaluation set for membership-inference attacks. The five VQA corpora, ScienceQA, MME-Perception and synthetic username/user-ID domain remain unchanged. The larger privacy subsets in Appendix E are a size ablation rather than a new domain.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates LOSS, Zlib Entropy and Min-k% Prob as attack comparators in Section 4.4 and Table 5. v1 discusses membership inference but does not evaluate these methods. The original Origin, ImageTransf. and TextTransf. controls are retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols measure gradients after 1, 10 and 100 updates, test a 13B backbone and LoRA rank 256, and increase privacy subsets from 5 to 100 items. The new MIA evaluation uses 100 member and 100 non-member examples, ROC AUC, and Qwen-VL fine-tuned on GQA at 100% privacy embedding. Original main-experiment settings remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained batch-size ablation, v2 tests persistence across multiple updates (Table 4), sensitivity to backbone size and LoRA rank (Tables 7–8), and privacy-subset size (Appendix E, Table 11). These substantially broaden the investigation of whether the observed gradient effects persist across training and capacity conditions.

E5.justification: Existing mean-plus/minus reporting and the 100-single-step comparison remain unchanged. New tables provide point estimates without introducing seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added update counts describe training duration, not independent repetitions.

E6.justification: v2 adds results in Tables 4, 5, 7, 8 and 11 while retaining the original benchmark, gradient and probing results. Table 4 reports privacy-gradient similarities of 92.9, 91.6 and 84.6 across 1, 10 and 100 updates. Table 5 reports before/after-fine-tuning AUCs of 50.7/49.9 for LOSS, 63.8/63.3 for Zlib Entropy and 53.5/53.2 for Min-k% Prob; these decrease slightly, contrary to the accompanying 'marginal increase' wording.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises Equation 9 to include covariance terms arising from shared sample means. It replaces the stated exact variance with an upper bound of 3 sigma_y^2 sigma_u^2/(B-1), updating Equation 10 accordingly. This is a localized mathematical revision; the Gaussian assumptions and claimed inverse-batch-size relationship remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, research questions and central memorization/probing contribution remain unchanged. The conclusion explicitly extends the claim about inaccessible memorized information from direct prompting to membership-inference attacks. Its added batch-size statement reiterates a claim already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting larger model capacity to stronger privacy sensitivity and larger privacy subsets to greater effort learning private information. It also interprets the new attack results as showing ineffective MIAs. These extend the retained spurious-correlation explanation and batch-size mitigation discussion without substantially revising applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 documents generating 20 attack examples per private item and, in Appendix E, generating 100 username/ID pairs per subset with duplicate checks after each generation. Existing training and probing hyperparameters, transformation instructions, prompts and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the evaluated attacks, attention visualization, association-based privacy leakage and autonomous-agent privacy evaluation, including Yeom, Shi, Zhang, Shao, Meng and Zharmagambetov. The related-work discussion expands modestly while retaining its central distinction between task-relevant privacy and task-irrelevant memorization.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. v2 inserts a MIA subsection, subdivides the ablation section, adds Appendix E and acknowledgements, and makes localized conclusion, author-name and running-header edits. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds five result tables covering training steps, MIAs, backbone size, LoRA rank and privacy-subset size. Figure 2 is redrawn with a flower example and attention heatmaps, and Figure 1 replaces displayed personal details with anonymous placeholders. Existing probing plots and appendix examples are retained, with tables and surrounding material repositioned.

improvement.justification: The new multi-update, capacity and privacy-diversity checks address limitations of v1's gradient diagnostics, while the MIA experiment directly tests the claimed difficulty of exposing memorized information. These modestly strengthen empirical support. The gains are limited by reporting and reasoning weaknesses: Section 4.4 contradicts Table 5's declining AUCs, and the revised Appendix A still uses a Chebyshev upper bound to claim a probability bounded away from zero. The core probing evidence remains unchanged.
